title: 1973 AHSME Problem 18
statement: If \(p\ge5\) is a prime number, then \(24\) divides \(p^2-1\) without remainder

solutions.text:
A prime \(p\ge5\) is odd, so \(p-1\) and \(p+1\) are consecutive even integers. One is divisible by \(4,\) making their product divisible by \(8.\) Among the three consecutive integers \(p-1,\) \(p,\) \(p+1,\) one is divisible by \(3.\) It cannot be \(p,\) since \(p\ge5\) is prime, so \(3\) also divides \((p-1)(p+1).\) Because \(3\) and \(8\) are relatively prime, \[ (p-1)(p+1)=p^2-1 \] is always divisible by \(24.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Among the three consecutive integers \(p-1,\) \(p,\) \(p+1,\) locate factors of \(3\) and \(8\)
